note: Starting points for Josh's Reboot 60A air plasma with a P-80 torch. Speeds, amps, air pressure and cut height come from the official PrimeWeld CUT60 cutting-speed table (a close equivalent 60 A air plasma). Pierce height uses the published P-80 note that pierce height is generally not less than 5 mm on thicker plate; thinner rows and all pierce delays, lead-ins, and thicker kerfs are estimates and are labelled as such. Always test on scrap and trim the values to suit the machine. Air pressure: read it at the plasma's own gauge with air flowing (press the torch test/purge), not at the compressor.

sources.title: PrimeWeld CUT60 Cutting Speed Reference Table (official user manual)
sources.what: Amps, air PSI, cut speed (IPM) and distance-to-work 0.06 in for mild steel, stainless and aluminium from 26 ga to 3/4 in. Converted here to mm and mm/min (× 25.4).
sources.also: The same table as a one-page PDF: https://forum.langmuirsystems.com/uploads/short-url/yLt8kbbpOWWVVRPmM4CL2HKpoxX.pdf

sources.title: P80 cutting parameters (Heavth)
sources.what: P-80 nozzle/current bands and 'piercing height (generally not less than 5 mm)'. 60 A is listed for 5–15 mm plate at 800–1600 mm/min (a range, not a per-thickness table). Air 5 bar.

sources.title: CUT-60 kerf, Langmuir Systems forum (May 2021)
sources.what: User-reported kerf of about 0.050 in (1.27 mm) on a CUT-60 with a 0.9 mm / 40 A tip, 1/4 in and thinner. Not an official chart.
